Description: Central server communicating with PLCs/RTUs and HMIs
Notes: Best single vantage point for commands reaching the process.

Description: Segments zones and controls traffic between IT/DMZ/OT
Notes: Cheapest high-value source. Confirms Purdue zone-crossing detections.

Description: Secure access point into OT network (RDP/SSH)
Notes: Every legitimate remote-access session should pass through here; alert on anything that does not.

Description: Secure remote connectivity into OT or between sites
Notes: Pairs with jump host logs for full remote-access chain visibility.

Description: Connects devices and defines OT network segments
Notes: Port security, MAC changes, VLAN hopping detection; volume manageable if filtered.

Description: Core automation controllers executing logic
Notes: High value but limited native logging; passive monitoring as proxy.

Description: Executes safety-critical logic with redundancy
Notes: Low volume but any event here is a priority-1 investigation regardless of source difficulty.

Description: Used for configuration, programming, diagnostics
Notes: Windows event logs are easy to collect; tune aggressively, usually the noisiest critical source.

Description: Protocol translation, aggregation, mirroring between zones
Notes: Good chokepoint for cross-protocol detections (e.g. Modbus-to-OPC UA translation abuse).

Description: Stores process data, events, alarms for analysis and business use
Notes: Easy win; also valuable for baselining process behavior, not just security events.

Description: Operator interface for monitoring and control
Notes: Watch for unauthorized setpoint changes, login anomalies, engineering-mode access outside change windows.

Description: Protection and control devices (mostly power sector)
Notes: IEC 61850 GOOSE/MMS visibility if available; otherwise rely on substation gateway logs.

Description: Routes traffic between OT network segments
Notes: Complements firewall logs for east-west traffic between cells/zones.

Description: Hosts ICS applications (analytics, alarms, reporting) on Windows/Linux
Notes: Standard Windows/Linux telemetry pipeline applies directly.

Description: Manages continuous processes in distributed control systems
Notes: Vendor-specific logging is limited; prioritize network-based detection.

Description: Advanced programmable controller with extended capabilities
Notes: Same constraints as PLC; passive monitoring is the practical path.

Description: Aggregates field data and forwards to SCADA
Notes: Geographically distributed, often serial-based; polling-based DNP3/104 monitoring recommended.

Description: Passive monitoring of OT protocols
Notes: Highest engineering effort but fills every visibility gap above; needs dedicated tuning and a Sigma/DPI ruleset.

Description: Directory services and identity providers used by OT users, systems, and remote access
Notes: Covers account lifecycle, privileged groups, policy, and authentication events; collect only OT-scoped identities and dependencies.

Description: Backups for SCADA, HMI, historian, EWS, and controller projects
Notes: Detect deletion, retention, or job-policy changes and provide recovery-readiness evidence during response.

Description: Sensors and actuators providing raw input/output
Notes: Do not attempt direct log collection; covered indirectly via PLC/RTU and process historian data.
